title: Competition-Level Code Generation with AlphaCode
authors: Y. Li, D. Choi, J. Chung, et al. (26 authors)
before: Code models produced one attempt per problem.
problem: Competitive programming problems are too hard to solve first try.
breakthrough: Generate a million candidate programs, filter by running the examples, and cluster to pick submissions.
why: An early argument that spending more compute at inference buys accuracy, which is the test-time compute thesis.
next: Self-consistency, verifier-guided search and eventually reasoning models.
inherits: Sampling widely and filtering, rather than trusting a single generation.
